Policy for Differently Abled Candidates

Procedure for Granting of Facility of Extra Time to Differently Abled Candidates
in Institute of Actuaries of India Examinations

Physically/Visually Challenged candidates appearing in the Institute of Actuaries of India Examinations requiring writer’s help/extra time are requested to adopt the following procedure:

Documents required with the application.

  1. Handwritten application in candidate’s own handwriting. In case candidate cannot write, then their representative may write on behalf of the candidate stating their relationship with the candidate
  2. Certified true copy of the Doctor’s Certificate (Civil Surgeon of Government hospital or of above level) stating that the disability is of permanent nature and its description.
  3. Certified true copies of the permission granted (if any) by the State higher secondary board/university towards his/her 10+2 or degree examinations he/she has appeared.
  4. Full size (Post card) photograph attested by the member of the Institute or by a Gazetted officer indicating name of the candidate on the photograph itself.
  5. Two colour passport size photographs taken within last 3 months for concession card.
  6. Supporting document of educational qualification etc of the writer (If any).

A minimum of half an hour shall be granted for diseases/disability subject to the approval of the application.

The application should reach the Institute before the closing date of the receipt of examination application form of the Institute.

Discontinuation of IAI ID card

Dear Students

Please be informed that with effect from 7th March 2017, the Institute has discontinued the issuance of IAI Photo Identity Cards as compulsory photo ID proof for its Examinations.

Going forward, the Institute will accept the following Government approved photo Identity Cards for its examinations as valid Identity proof along with the Hall Ticket:

  1. Passport
  2. Pan card
  3. Driving license
  4. Aadhar Card
  5. Voter ID card

Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) shall grant exemptions to students who fulfil the eligibility criteria as mentioned below for old curriculum subjects i.e. Core Technical, Core Applications and Specialist Technical subjects and also for new curriculum subjects i.e. Core Principles, Core Practices and Specialist Principles Subjects.

Institute and Faculty of Actuaries

IAI shall grant exemptions if the students have passed Institute and Faculty of Actuaries exams from 1st January 2019 until 31st December 2021.
IAI shall grant exemption to students who have passed Core Technical Subjects (CT), Core Principles subjects (CS1, CS2, CM1, CM2, CB1, CB2 and CB3), Core Applications Subjects (CA), Core Practices (CP), and Specialist Technical (ST) and Specialist Principles (SP) Subjects from Institute and Faculty of Actuaries. Students will be awarded exemption from the corresponding IAI Exam

Also, Institute shall not grant exemptions to CA2 subjects passed from IFoA from September 2018 to December 2018 exam sessions and to CP3 subject passed from September 2017 to December 2018 exam sessions.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

1. How can I get exemption for SA level subjects?
IAI does not have exemption arrangement for SA Level subject as these are country specific (India) subjects.
2. I have cleared 103 (old syllabus) so which is the subject as per the current syllabus and can I get exemption for that subject?
Current subject CT4 is inclusive of 103 and 104. Thus if you have cleared old subject 103 and 104 then only you are eligible to get exemption from CT4.
3. When was the last exam for 103 and 104 - old subjects conducted?
The last exam for 103 and 104 was conducted in November 2006.
4. I have passed CT1 (CM1) from IFoA but have not taken their student membership. Can I get exemption with IAI?
IAI shall grant exemption for CT1 (CM1) passed from IFoA only after you have taken their student membership.

fellow.title: Fellow
fellow.html:
This is to inform you that the Change of Category (COC) application process has been transitioned entirely to an online mode.

Members who meet the eligibility criteria for Fellowship are requested to log in to their IAI account and access the 'Change of Category' module to submit their applications.

Please note the following:

  • It is mandatory to fill in all required details accurately.
  • The applicable fees must be remitted online during the application process.
  • Offline applications will no longer be accepted.

We appreciate your cooperation in embracing this digital transition

There are mainly two routes, VIZ.,examination and MRA through which a student/ Associate member can apply for fellowship after qualifying/exemption of all Core Principle series (CS 1 & CS2, CM1 & CM2,CB1,CB2,CB3, all Core Application series (CP1 to CP3), any two of Core Principles series (SP1, SP2, SP3, SP4, SP5, SP7, SP8, SP9) and any one of Specialist Application series (SA1, SA2,SA3, SA4 & SA5) with additional conditions depending on the application route:

1.Fellowship (IAI Examination Route)- Conditions

  • Should be current student member of IAI
  • Minimum 3 years of work based actuarial experience*
  • Attended India Fellowship Seminar (Validity - to be admitted as FIAI within 24 Months - counted from the month immediately succeeding the month of successful attending IFS Seminar) [Ref : IFS Principle Document (ver. 2.02/May 2012)]

2.Fellowship (Mutual Recognition Agreement Route-Other than IFoA, UK)- Conditions

  • Should be Fellow member of The Institute of Actuaries of Australia and The Casualty Actuarial Society
  • Confirmation from parent body that:
    • He/She has attained fellowship by examination route
    • His/Her subscription is up to date
    • There is no Public Disciplinary sanction imposed against him/her
  • Work Experience :
    • Have been ‘ordinarily resident’ in India for at least one year and have gained suitable actuarial experience in India (For Institute of Actuaries of Australia)
    • Three years period of substantive practical General Insurance Actuarial Work Experience whether pre or post FCAS qualification within the six year period immediately prior to the application for FIAI status (For Casualty Actuarial Society)
  • India Fellowship Seminar :Attended India Fellowship Seminar (Validity - to be admitted as FIAI within 24 Months - counted from the month immediately succeeding the month of successful attending IFS Seminar) [Ref : IFS Principle Document (ver. 2.02/May 2012)]

Clarifications on experience:

  • Actuarial experience involving actuarial science as defined under section 2(1) (a) of the Actuaries Act, 2006 shall be considered for fellowship. The member should provide evidence of the experience and should justify that it involves application of actuarial science. (Decision taken in Council meeting dated 19th March 2016)
  • Council vide in its meeting dated 25th March 2017 has decided that experience in General Insurance to be considered to include experience in Health Insurance.

Format of experience certificate should have the following:

  • Must be printed on Company Letterhead
  • Name and Designation
  • Period of Actuarial Work
  • Brief description of Job profile Actuarial related work* and nature of work handled during the period e.g. Department, Responsibilities etc.
  • Must be signed by H R Manager or your Immediate Authority

3. Fellowship (Mutual Recognition Agreement Route-IFoA, UK)- Conditions

  • The candidate should have attained Fellowship of the IFOA by completing the qualification requirements of IFOA (not solely in recognition of membership of another actuarial association)
  • Should have entitled to practise as a member of the IFOA
  • In the event that there is no work experience requirement built into Fellowship of IFOA, which have completed, as at the date of your application, at least three years post-qualification practical work-based experience of actuarial practice
  • Have undertaken a professionalism course as prescribed by IFOA ; and
  • Authorisation to submit in writing for IFOA to release relevant records to the IAI concerning any adverse disciplinary determination, finding, sanction and/or penalty, to which you been subject, in accordance with the IAI’s disciplinary process.

4. Fellowship (Affiliate to Fellow)- Conditions

  • Confirmation from parent body that:
  • He/She has attained fellowship by examination route. (Where IAI has Mutual Recognition Agreement)
  • His/Her subscription is up to date
  • There is no Public Disciplinary sanction imposed against him/her
  • Work Experience : (a) Have been ‘ordinarily resident’ in India for at least one year and have gained suitable actuarial experience in India (For Institute of Actuaries of Australia)
  • Three years period of substantive practical General Insurance Actuarial Work Experience whether pre or post FCAS qualification within the six year period immediately prior to the application for FIAI status (For Casualty Actuarial Society)
  • India Fellowship Seminar :Attended India Fellowship Seminar (Validity - to be admitted as FIAI within 24 Months - counted from the month immediately succeeding the month of successful attending IFS Seminar) [Ref : IFS Principle Document (ver. 2.02/May 2012)]

Application Form for admission as Affiliate Member

Honorary Fellow Member

The Council may, by a vote of not less than four-fifths of all its members, admit as an honorary member, a person who, on account of his eminence and his experience in matters related to the profession of actuary is considered to be able to render assistance in promoting the objects of the Institute provided that he is not practicing as an Actuary. The person to be considered for such admission shall satisfy all the requirements prescribed by the Council and duly approved by a General meeting of the Institute from time to time. An honorary member shall not have any rights to vote on any matter or resolution in any meeting of the Institute.

frequently-asked-questions-0.title: Frequently Asked Questions
frequently-asked-questions-0.html:
1. What is the duration of the examination?

The students are advised to take the exam in less than 2 hours.

2. How many questions will be asked?

There will be 32 questions asked.

3. What is the pass mark?

Students need to get 75% of the pass mark i.e. get 24 questions correct out of 32 questions in order to clear the examination.

4. How will the results declared?

Results will be declared on the 10th of every month or the next working day.

5. Will the students get feedback from the exam?.

Yes, there is an online feedback. However students are not allowed to take any screenshot or save this feedback in any other manner.

6. What happens if there is no internet access, or sound on PCs? What happens if your internet connection is slow?

We expect students to find ways of getting suitable internet access while engaged in the course.

7. What will be the Exam Centre?

There is no examination centre for the CB3 exam. You can appear this examination where you can have a good quality of internet access.

8. What if I do not clear the online exam?

You can retake the examination within a gap of 31 days of your previous attempt upto 6 months starting from the date of online examination. You need not register again to retake the exam.

If you have any queries about Examination please email us at exam@actuariesindia.org

frequently-asked-questions-1.title: Frequently Asked Questions
frequently-asked-questions-1.html:
Frequently Asked Questions(FAQs)

⌕

General

01 I have passed ACET. What do I do next? +

If you have passed the ACET, this means you are eligible for Candidate membership of the IAI. Click on the following link to fill the Online Admission related details Click Here

02 Where can I find more information on the syllabus? +

Syllabus may be obtained from Institute’s website Click Here

03 How many subjects can I attempt in one examination cycle? +

There is no limit; Candidates can register for multiple exams in an exam session provided they do not fall on same date and time.

04 What are the dates of actuarial exams? +

Actuarial exams are conducted twice a year – usually May and November. Examination dates for the upcoming exams are posted on the Institute website Click Herefor further details.

05 From where can I appear for an Actuarial Exams? +

Institute has taken the initiative of conducting Centre based online Actuarial exams November 2026 onwards.

Click Hereto view the centre list.

* If a candidate wishes to request an examination centre other than those currently available, they may raise a Centre Request through their Member Login > Centre Request Form. The Institute will review the request and take the necessary action, subject to feasibility and availability.

06 Do the answer scripts accrue negative marking? +

No, there is no negative marking.

07 How does the Institute ensure that examination marking is fair, consistent and accurate before declaring the final results? +

The Institute follows a structured marking and review process to ensure consistency, fairness, and transparency in the assessment of examination answer scripts, in accordance with the applicable Pass Mark Rules for the respective subject and level.

Each answer script is independently assessed by two examiners with further review by a Review Examiner, wherever applicable as part of the Institute’s quality assurance process.

For scripts not referred to a Review Examiner, the average of the marks awarded by the two examiners is considered the final mark; where a script is referred for review the Review Examiner’s marks are considered final for determining the candidate’s result.

08 What is the pattern of the examinations - is it objective or subjective? +

Beginning November 2025 examinations, the assessments for CB1, CB2, CB3, CS1A, CS2A, CM1A, and CM2A will consist of both Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs) and descriptive (non-MCQ) components. The MCQ section will account for a minimum of 20% and a maximum of 30% of the total marks, while the remaining marks will be allocated to the descriptive/subjective section.

09 How do I prepare myself for the exams – is there a provision for coaching at IAI? +

Institute has a robust mechanism for coaching and counselling our Candidates. Click Hereto view the details related to coaching.

10 Which order I should follow when sitting for exams? +

While there is no prescribed order, it is seen that starting the actuarial exams with Core principles works well in easing the Candidates’ understanding and logical follow through with the exam rigour. A general thumb rule based on trends indicates that Candidates follow a numerical order. It may be worth noting that:

CB1 – Business Finance assumes knowledge of CM1
CS2 – Actuarial Statistics assumes knowledge of CS1
CM2 – Economic Modelling assumes knowledge of CS1, CS2, CM1 and CB2
CB3- Business Management has no formal prerequisites, but taking it early can support better understanding of the business and professional context of actuarial work

- You may also consider your academic background when selecting subjects. Typically preferred choices based on education background have been:

Academic Background Subjects that may be considered
Management CB3
Mathematics / Engineering CM1
Statistics CS1 and CS2
Economics CB2
Accounts / Commerce CB1
11 11. Is there a compulsory order for Core Principles subjects? +

There is no compulsory order in which Core Principles subjects must be studied or attempted. The subject numbering broadly represents an order that may be appropriate for Candidate working in life insurance or pensions.

You may choose a different sequence depending on their area of interest or career:

  • Candidates working in general insurance may prefer to take CS2 after CM1.
  • Candidates working in investment may prefer to take CB2 and CM2 before CS2 and CM1.
  • CB3 can be taken at any stage and may be particularly useful early in the qualification, as it develops an understanding of business-related solutions and practical, work-based skills.
  • Ultimately, candidates should select their examination sequence based on their academic background, prior knowledge, area of actuarial interest, and individual study plan.
12 How much time does it take to prepare for a particular exam? +
  • Candidates - The time required to prepare for an examination varies from candidate to candidate and depends on factors such as individual commitment, prior knowledge, academic background and study approach. However, based on the experience of successful Candidates, the following may be considered as a broad guide to the intensive study hours generally required:
  • Core Principles (CS1 & CS2, CM1 & CM2, CB1 & CB2): Approximately 125–150 hours, depending on the candidate’s prior educational background and familiarity with the subject.
  • Business Management (CB3): At least 20 hours.
  • Actuarial Practice (CP1): Approximately 400 hours.
  • Model Practice (CP2): Approximately 50 hours.
  • Communication Practice (CP3): Approximately 50 hours.
  • Specialist Principles (SP): Approximately 200 hours.
  • Specialist Applications (SA): Approximately 300 hours.

Note: These figures are intended as indicative guidelines only, and candidates should plan their preparation based on their individual circumstances and level of familiarity with the subject.

13 What is considered as prior knowledge during CP2/CP3 examination? +

Candidates- For CP2 and CP3, Candidates are expected to have prior knowledge of the relevant CS, CM and CB subjects.
- Where a question requires any information beyond the assumed knowledge from these subjects, the relevant additional information will be provided within the question paper, wherever applicable.

14 Can I appear for CP1 in the beginning? +

There is no minimum eligibility requirement for attempting CP1. However, Candidates may find it more beneficial - to clear all Core Principle subjects before attempting CP1.

15 What is the eligibility for applying for CP2 & CP3 subjects? +

There are no pre-requisites of clearing other subject papers in order to register for CP2 & CP3.

16 Is there a Policy for Differently Abled Candidates -appearing for - the Examination? +

Yes, Institute has a policy for differently abled candidates that outlines the applicable provisions. Candidates may refer the below link: Click Herefor details.

17 Can I use an External Calculator from - IAI approved list during online examination? +

Yes, you may use scientific calculators during the examination, as applicable. However, only the following models from the IAI approved list are permitted:

  1. Casio FX-82 MS / SOLAR / SX Plus / ES (with or without any suffix)
  2. Casio FX-83 (ES/MS) (with or without any suffix)
  3. Casio FX-85 (ES/MS) (with or without any suffix)
  4. Casio FX-220 Plus
  5. Casio FX-350 MS
  6. Casio FX-570 MS
  7. Canon F-502 G
  8. Canon F-715 S / SG
  9. Canon F-720i
  10. HP 10s+
  11. Sharp EL-501 X
  12. Sharp EL-503 W
  13. Sharp EL-506 X / W
  14. Sharp EL-509 X / W
  15. Sharp EL-510 RN
  16. Sharp EL-520 X / W
  17. Sharp EL-531 XH / XG / WH (with or without any suffix)
  18. TI-30X IIS / IIB
  19. TI-30 eco RS / Xa
  20. TI-36X II
  21. Texas Instruments BA II Plus (with or without any suffix)
  22. Texas Instruments TI-30 Plus (with or without any suffix)
  23. Hewlett Packard HP12c (with or without any suffix)

Please note: You will not be permitted to use any other model of calculator during the examination.

You may be required to show the calculator to the invigilator for verification and validation during the examination.

18 How long does it take to become an Actuary? Is there a specific timeframe within which the examinations must be completed? +

There is no fixed duration for completing the Actuarial. Candidates are free to appear for the examinations at a pace that suits their individual circumstances. 13 subjects are prescribed to be cleared before one is awarded the Fellowship and calls for continued and sustained efforts to complete the course. Additionally, you need a minimum of three years’ relevant work experience to qualify as a Fellow and must have successfully attended the India Fellowship Seminar (IFS), which must be valid at the time of admission as a Fellow (Validity - to be admitted as FIAI within 24 Months - counted from the month immediately succeeding the month of successful attending IFS Seminar). Considering the examination requirements, work experience, and other Fellowship criteria, the typical timeframe to qualify as an Actuary in recent years has been approximately 5–8 years.

19 Do I need to work before I qualify? How do I work as an actuary if I have not yet qualified? +

Yes.To qualify as a Fellow, you are required to have a minimum of three years of relevant work experience in an Actuarial field. Almost all reputable actuarial employers offers attractive study support programs to support your development and growth. These may include study leave for preparing for and appearing in examinations, mentoring and guidance from by senior and experience colleagues and financial assistance towards as well as financial support. Actuarial qualification is a professional qualification, and gaining relevant practical work experience alongside your studies is an important part of the qualification journey. Typically, -once you have cleared two to four core technical subjects, it is advisable to start exploring - your preferred career options and secure an opportunity in actuarial field.

20 Where and how can I get a job? +

There are several ways to find a job in the actuarial filed.

  • The Institute’s website provides a list of potential actuarial employers in India.
  • Career opportunities are regularly shared in the Actuary India magazine as well posted on the Institute’s website. Many reputed Insurance companies and actuarial consultancies - hire Candidates for entry level actuarial positions, Candidates open to University graduates with no or very few actuarial exams pass.

Candidates- The Institute also has a Placement Cell that helps members find their first job. It provides guidance and connects Candidates with different actuarial employers. The Placement Cell also helps Candidates understand the skills and training required for available job opportunities. Members can register with the Placement Cell to get support for finding a job or changing jobs.

Kindly contact Ms. Binita Rautela atbinita@actuariesindia.org / +912262433342 for placement support

21 Can I skip an exam or choose not to appear a particular exam session? +

Yes, you can. However, you must ensure that your IAI membership remains active and up to date.

22 What certifications do I get after clearing the various levels? +

You can find detailed information regarding the certifications is available at the Institute’s website Types of Membership

23 What if I fail to appear in either of Paper A orPaper B for subjects CS1, CS2, CM1, CM2, CP1 and CP2? +

Result will be Absent for respective subject.

24 Are the examinations conducted in an Open-Book format? +

No, this is a closed book examination.

25 Is there a change in CB3 – Business Management exam format? +

Yes. From November 2024, CB3 – Business Management exam is aligned with the actuarial examination process. This change eliminates the pre-requisite of Business game and pre-course assignment before the exam. The exam consists of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and has a duration of 90 minutes.

26 How many attempts do I get for CB3 – Business Management under new exam format? +

From November 2024, Candidate gets one attempt per exam session. If a Candidate does not pass the exam, they can register and appear for the exam again in a subsequent session, just like other actuarial exams.

Examination Guidelines

27 Where can I find detailed information on how to appear for the Actuarial Examination? +

Detailed information regarding the examination process, instructions, rules, and guidelines is available in the Candidate Guide for Actuarial Examination.

28 What is the duration of the examination? +

For centre Based online Examination, each paper is 3 hours and 15 minutes, except CS1B, CS2B, CM1B & CM2B each which are 1 hour and 45 minutes and CB3 will be of90 minutes

For Paper A & B of CS, CM and CP2, Candidates must keep track of the the exam timer themselves. An additional 15 minutes is provided for uploading the answer script and the upload option will be available within the platform. Any written work done in- the answer script during additional 15 minutes may lead to loss of attempt or failure in uploading the answer script.

The last successfully uploaded answer script in exam platform will be considered for evaluation. Reference image is as below:

29 Is there any risk of examination misconduct by Candidates while writing examinations online? +

Yes. Candidates must follow the Candidate Guide for Actuarial Examination and all examination rules. The Institute reserves the right to take appropriate action if any misconduct is identified during or after the examination.

30 Can I use Actuarial Table during examination? +

You must bring your own actuarial tables to the Examination centre for the subjects where they are applicable. The Institute will not provide actuarial tables. The actuarial table should be free from any annotation,markings - or any pre-written loose sheets attached to it. -The Invigilator may ask you to show the Actaurial table book for verification before or during the examination. (Note: Print or xerox copy is not allowed)

31 How - should I write the solutions or responses to the questions? +

The approach for writing solutions or responses may vary by subject. The subject wise approach is provided below:

Subject Approach to Write Solution
CB1, CB2, CB3
  • To type answers in Text Editor within the exam platform.
  • For MCQ, select the correct response(s) available within the exam platform.
CS & CM (Paper A)
  • To type answers in MS Word and upload in the exam platform.
  • For MCQ, select the correct response(s) available within the exam platform.
CS (Paper B) To copy & paste the R codes and output in an MS Word document and upload in the exam platform.
CP2, CM (Paper B) Download the Solution Template (Excel) embedded within the question and then upload the worked solution template back to the exam platform.
CP3, SP, SA To type answers in Text Editor within the exam platform.
32 How should I write the solutions or responses to MCQ type questions? +

Select the correct option(s) from the choices displayed - on right hand side of the examination screen.

33 Is there any specific font or font size to use while answering through online mode of Examination? Can I use bold, italics or coloured text in my answer scripts? +

It is recommended to use default font size.

34 What happens if the examination platform fails during the examination? +

If the examination platform fails due to an issue not related to the candidate’s hardware, software or power or internet connectivity, the Institute will make reasonable efforts to provide an alternative arrangement.. If this is not possible, the Institute may reschedule the examination to another date or cancel the session or provide refund of examination fees, as appropriate.

35 What can I keep with me during the examination? +

The following are permitted during the examination:

  • Personal Keyboard (optional)
  • Personal Wired Mouse (optional)
  • Hardcopy of Hall ticket
  • Actuarial table book, where applicable
  • Scientific calculator, where applicable
  • Blank loose sheets for rough work.
  • Pen/Pencil for writing on the loose sheets
  • One government-issued ID for verification

The following are strictly not allowed during the examination: Any form of personal consumables, mobile phone , smart watches, smart glasses, handsfree devices, headsets/ earphones etc. or any other electronic gadgets.

36 What if I do not have a Government approved ID card and the hard copy of the hall ticket - with me at the time of Examination? +

You will not be allowed to appear for examination and may lose your examination attempt.

37 Can I request - a change to my examination start time? +

No. Examinations will be conducted as per the published Exam Timetable, and requests to change the examination time will not be accepted.

38 How to access "R Studio" for CS Paper B Subjects during examination? +

RStudio will be available on the local computer system provided at the examination centre and can be accessed during the examination.

39 How can I copy/paste codes and output from R Studio to MS Word? +

Type the codes and Output in “R Studio” and simply copy the content using Ctrl + C and to paste using Ctrl + V in MS Word document. In case Ctrl + V is not responding, try pasting by clicking the Paste à Paste Special à Values option under Home tab within the Command Bar in MS Word application.

40 How to access "Excel" or "Word" application during examination? +

Microsoft Excel or Word can be accessed and used on the local computer system provided at the examination centre. Note: This is only applicable for CM1A,CM2A,CS1A,CS2A, CS1B, CS2B, CM1B, CM2B and CP2 Subjects.

41 How to toggle between the Examination Window and MS Word/Excel during the examination? +

You can use ALT+TAB to toggle between the Examination Window and MS Word/ MS Excel/ RStudio during the examination.
Note: This is only applicable for CM1A,CM2A,CS1A, CS2A, CS1B, CS2B, CM1B, CM2B and CP2 Subjects.

42 How to insert Equations/Symbols in solution typing area? +

You can insert equation in solution typing area using the equation editor available in the exam platform for all subjects except for CS Series, CM Series and CP2 Subject. Kindly refer following link - https://support.mettl.com/portal/en/kb/articles/how-to-attempt-math-and-chemistry-type-questions-in-the-test

43 Will there be questions in CP1, CP3, SP and SA subjects that require graphs and diagrams in the solution? +

Our examiners have aligned the question paper pattern where you will not have a mandatory requirement to use graphs/diagrams to support your answers.

44 What should I do if I am not able to locate the file for upload? +

If your answerscript is in a Word or Excel file, open it and go to File > Info. The file location is usually displayed at the top or under the document properties section.

45 What should I do if I am unable to upload my answer script in the last 15 minutes of the examination? +

The last 15 minutes of the examination are reserved only to upload the answerscript. You must use this time only to upload the answerscript. Any working done or making changes to your answerscript during last 15 minutes may lead to loss of attempt or failure to upload the answer script. The last successfully uploaded answer script in the examination platform -will be considered for evaluation.

If you face any technical issue that prevents you from uploading your script, immediately contact the available Invigilator for assistance.
Note: Do not seek support from any other member including friends or family for uploading the answer script or resolving any technical issue.

frequently-asked-questions-4.title: Frequently Asked Questions
frequently-asked-questions-4.html:
1. What's the IAI SOA IFRI Certificate Program?

Answer: It's a collaboration between the Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) and the Society of Actuaries (SOA), offering comprehensive learning in the principles and practices of financial reporting under IFRS17 standards, particularly for the insurance sector.

2. Who should consider this program?

Answer: This program is designed for individuals actively involved in IFRS implementation within the insurance sector. It's also beneficial for professionals working with actuarial or finance functions, especially in insurance companies, financial, accounting, and audit firms.

3. How is the program structured?

Answer: It's a five-month program, including six e-learning online modules, two half-day virtual instructor-led seminars, and a final assessment. Successful participants receive a professional certificate jointly from IAI and SOA 

4. How many hours does it take to complete the e-learning module?

Answer: Typically, each e-learning module requires approximately 20-30 hours for completion.

5. Who can register for the certificate program?

Answer: Any IAI member and non-member resident in India can register for the certificate program. (While the program is open to non-members, it is recommended that candidates possessing strong understanding of actuarial, or accounting concepts only register for the course. A formal qualification in actuarial science, accounting or finance will be desirable). 

6. How much does the certificate program cost?

Answer:

Fee for Members

₹ 65,000 plus 18% GST extra

Fee for Non-Members

₹ 81,250 plus 18% GST extra
7. When does the 1st program start and how long does it last?

Answer: The program is expected to start in January 2024, (access of e-learning modules will be from 22nd January to 22nd June 2024), with live virtual seminar and assessment in June 2024.

8. What is the mode of conduct of the certificate program?

Answer: Online.

9. Is there a certification exam at the end of the program?

Answer: Yes

10. How do I register?

Answer: Click Here: https://elearning.actuariesindia.org/ . The registrations are on first-come-first-served basis. You can register online, and instructions will be sent upon successful registration.

11. Who will be the instructors for the Seminar?

Answer: The seminars will be led by fellow members of IAI who are highly proficient and knowledgeable in their respective specialized fields.

12. Are there any prerequisites for joining the program?

Answer: No specific prerequisites are required, but a background in actuarial, finance, accounting or related fields is beneficial.

13. How will the online sessions be conducted, and what platform will be used?

Answer: The online sessions will be conducted using a dedicated e-learning platform. Participants will receive detailed instructions on accessing and participating in the virtual sessions.

14. What is the recommended device for accessing the modules?

Answer: For an enhanced user experience, it is recommended to access the modules using a computer/laptop rather than a mobile device.

15. Can a viewed video under the module be reviewed?

Answer: Yes, there are no review limitations. Registrants may move back and forth throughout the module as they wish.

frequently-asked-questions.title: Frequently Asked Questions
frequently-asked-questions.html:
1. How frequently will the entrance exam be held?

The exam will be held two times in a year tentatively in months of June and December.

2. How much is the registration fee?

The registration fee for the entrance exam ₹. 3,000 (three thousand only). This covers the cost of one Sample Question Paper, Indicative Solution and Online Exam. The registration fee once paid is neither refundable nor can it be carried forward for the next ACET. You are therefore requested to make considered decision to take up the examination and only then register.

3. Will the Question paper have sectional cut offs? What is the Pass mark for ACET Examination?

The Question paper will not have any sectional cut offs. The Pass mark for ACET Examination is 50%. Acet_register_form: Link

4. Do the reference books cover the ACET syllabus?

The reference books are for guidance purpose and they may or may not cover the given ACET syllabus.

5. How can I register for the exam? Please mention step by step process, if possible.

IMPORTANT NOTE: While registering, kindly use Browsers, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome and Internet Explorer (7+ higher version). Please do not use mobile phone for registration. The fields marked with a red asterisk are compulsory and cannot be left blank.
Step 1 - Go to IAI website and signup at Acet_register_form
Step 2 - Fill up the online registration form and make the payment online. Before you make the payment, make sure all your details are correct because no subsequent changes would be possible thereafter.
Step 3 - On successful completion of payment, you will also receive an e- mail at your registered e-mail address confirming your registration and successful payment. (Inform us immediately, in case, you do not receive it). Kindly take a printout of your ACET online Registration Form.

6. Can payment be made by any other means instead of online payment?

You can only register for the exam by making an online payment.

7. How do I get my examination Hall Ticket?

It will be available in your login at the below mentioned link:-
Acet_login

8. Is there any penalty (Negative Marking) for wrong answers?

Negative marking has been discontinued from September 2019 Examination. There is no negative marking for wrong answers.

9. When will the results be declared?

The results are normally declared within 10 working days’ time from the date of the exam. The results would be available on the IAI website.

10. What happens after passing the exam?

If you are amongst the successful candidates, you need to follow the online admission process. (Available on the IAI Website). Note that your membership acceptance would be subject to production of attested true copies of your education certificates that would be subject to independent verification within the timelines specified. Also once your membership is accepted and you receive the student membership ID, you can subscribe for the study material of your selected Core principle subjects online. You can then apply for the Regular Actuarial Examinations.
• Note : Validity of ACET results is only for three years from the date of declaration of exam result for taking student membership of IAI.

11. How will IAI contact me after registration?

Please see Q5 for details of the registration procedure. If you don’t receive any communication from IAI after the registration process, please contact the ACET Helpdesk at acet@actuariesindia.org.

12. Can I appear for a paper based exam?

Currently IAI offers this exam only in a Computer based format.

13. I live outside India. Can I appear for IAI ACET examination?

Yes. You can appear for IAI ACET examination from outside India also.

14. Can an examinee take more than one attempt at this exam?

Students who have been unsuccessful (for whatever reasons) can reappear by registering again for ACET.

15. Who do I contact if I don’t get the email from IAI or if the registration process fails?

Please contact the ACET HELPDESK acet@actuariesindia.org at the earliest.

16. Does Institute provides study material for ACET Examination?

Institute does not provide any study material for ACET Examination. However you can refer the Past ACET question papers with solution available under ACET Tab and name of the reference books available under ACET Syllabus tab.

17. What are the specifications for a photograph?
Dos Donts
Upload your recent standard passport size photograph (4.5 cm length x 3.5 cm width) in colour Do not upload black and white photographs
Background of the photograph should be plain white and the dress should be in dark colour Photograph with dark background or in uniform, or with eyes hidden under coloured or dark glasses will not be accepted
Photograph should fit within the given box Photograph is NOT to be signed
Frontal view of the full face should be visible in the photograph Distracting shadows on the face or on the background should not be there
Print of the photograph should be clear and with a continuous-tone quality Eyes must not be covered by hair.
Expression of the face should be natural (no grinning, frowning or raised eyebrows) Glares on eyeglasses should be avoided with a slight upward or downward tilt of the head
Eyes must be open and both edges of face must be clearly visible Photograph should not be damaged, for example: torn, creased, or marked
Minimum photo resolution should be of 150px *150px. Maximum photo size should not be more than 1MB to be saved only in (.png, .jpg, .bmp, .jpeg, .gif, .raw) format Head coverings are not permitted except for religious reasons, but the facial features from bottom of chin to top of forehead and both edges of the face must be clearly visible
Head should be in the centre of the frame and both ears should be visible Photographs cut from group photographs are not acceptable
18. Whether 12th appeared student can appear for the ACET examination?

Yes, but after passing ACET, at the time of applying for IAI student membership, the student should have qualified 12th standard.

19. Where can I find the Registration link for ACET Examination on website?

Please go to following link

20. Is there any provision of Revaluation or detailed mark sheet of ACET answers sheets?

For ACET Examination, there is no such provision.

21. If the registration fails and amount gets debited from account then whom to contact?

Please contact to IAI accounts department. Their contact details are available under contact us tab on IAI website Contact Us.

22 What is the mode of examination? Is it online or offline?

Currently IAI is conducting ACET examination in Home based online Format.

23. Will there be a change in structure of question paper?

ACET Question format remains the same as mentioned in ACET background

ACET Exam Structure
24 Where can I look for syllabus for the exam?

Please refer Syllabus tab at syllabus

25. Can I use External Calculator from approved list of IAI during online examination?

Yes, you may use scientific calculators during the examination as applicable. However, only the following models are permitted:

general-information-softcopy-material-0.html:
The soft copy of the study material shall be in eBook format which can be accessed by using Vital Source Bookshelf.

The process of ordering and accessing eBook is as under;

  • Member need to order the softcopy study material online through their IAI member login.
  • After making successful payment, member will receive receipt of payment and a unique code for the subject/s purchased on their registered email id. The unique code (token) is for one time use and should not be shared with any other person.
  • Member need to download Bookshelf for Mac/PC/iOS/Android from http://www.vitalsource.com/downloads .
  • Member has to create a Bookshelf account on http://www.vitalsource.com/redeem once he/she receives the unique code from IAI.
  • Sign in with your Bookshelf account email address and password.
  • Click "Redeem” on the respective subject and enter your code.
  • Click on "All Titles" in the collection pane to view all the books in your account.
  • Double click on the title to download the book. Once downloaded, double-click again to open the book.

Instructions:

  • The token once consumed cannot be returned or replaced.
  • The eBook validity after redemption, is 3 years online access and perpetual offline access
  • For any technical difficulties in opening , the members should follow the help and
  • support issued by Vital Source (outlined in the eBook redemption instructions)
  • Price list of soft copy material is given below in Annexure 1

VitalSource Bookshelf

eBooks are accessed using VitalSource Bookshelf.

Bookshelf enables students to access eBooks online through a browser or they can be downloaded to a laptop or mobile devices using the Bookshelf application or mobile app (for up- to-date versions of iOS, Android and Amazon Kindle Fire).

A Bookshelf eBook can be accessed on up to 4 authorised devices (2 laptops / PCs + 2 mobile devices, for example a work computer, a personal computer, a mobile phone and an iPad).

If using a company computer or device, students need to check they have permission to install the required application.

When printing from Bookshelf an automatic watermark will be added to every page. This cannot be removed as it is part of the software settings. The software will only let you print 100 pages each time you log into your account. The print quality is unlikely to be as high as a printed hard copy from IAI.

If students have any technical difficulties members should follow the help and support issued by Vital Source (outlined in the eBook redemption instructions). The IAI should not be held responsible for any technical issues experience by the members.

For any queries or assistance, contact us at kiran@actuariesindia.org/ 022 62433374

iai-accreditation-program.title: IAI Accreditation Program
iai-accreditation-program.html:
IAI Accreditation Program: Scaling the Actuarial Landscape with Trust and Inclusivity

It fills us with an immense pride, deep sense of responsibility and professional probity to introduce the transformative IAI Accreditation Program. A remarkable initiative exclusively designed for a holistic growth in actuarial education and profession. The objective of Accreditation programme is to nurture and enable a university/ institution curate courses with existing syllabi which has been mapped to that of IAI or the IAI syllabus itself! This allows the flexibility for institutions to innovate in both programme content and assessment methods, including coursework, also allowing for the programme to include aspects of actuarial research. This innovative program not only aligns with the core objectives of the Institution, but also serves as a driving force in strengthening the Actuarial Science realm.

Institute of Actuaries was established under the Actuaries Act 2006 for regulation of profession in India. One of the objects of the Institute is to promote the status of Actuarial Profession.

The Goals of Accreditation: At the heart of the IAI Accreditation Program lie its pivotal objectives:

  1. To achieve better quality education by diverting the focus from passing exams to an approach that places greater emphasis on the education.
  2. The University/Institute program are taught by people skilled in subject matter of early examinations.
  3. Increased ability to attract the best and brightest candidates to the actuarial profession.
  4. Enhanced relationship between IAI and respective Universities/Institution.
  5. Travel time through the examinations may be reduced.

The IAI Accreditation Program gets inclusive and is now open to diverse institutions:

Category A:  Universities and Educational Institutions offering Actuarial Science courses and allied courses can choose the mode of control mechanism for Core level subjects.

Accreditation framework:

  1. Exemptions for Aligned Programs: Exemptions for examinations aligned with Undergraduate, Postgraduate, and Diploma programs related to Actuarial Science and allied subjects. 
  2. Guidance and Standardization: Program extends guidance to standardize relevant educational courses to align seamlessly with IAI syllabus objectives.
  3. Enhancing Infrastructure: We're resolute towards augmenting and maintaining academic and physical infrastructure of exceptional quality.
  4. Elevating Examination Quality: Our commitment involves upgrading and maintaining examination processes to ensure unparalleled quality.
  5. Creating Centres of Excellence: We're actively engaged in developing Actuarial Centres of Excellence within institutions, designed to serve as cornerstone of guidance and support to actuarial candidates.
  6. Undertaking Research Projects: The program propels us forward in undertaking impactful research projects within Actuarial Science and its related areas.

Who can Apply: 

Universities and Educational Institutions offering Actuarial Science courses and allied courses can choose the mode of control mechanism for core level subjects.

To qualify, institutions should offer relevant courses, maintain a minimum number of student members, and adhere to specified criteria.

Navigating the Accreditation Assessment Model for Category A Institutions:

The IAI's Accreditation Assessment Model offers accredited institutions the flexibility to choose the assessment approach that best suits their needs while maintaining rigorous evaluation standards. This model ensures a balance between institutional autonomy and centralized assessment processes, ultimately contributing to the quality of actuarial education.

Subject-wise Control Mechanism:

Institutions have the flexibility to determine the assessment model for each subject based on their preferences and requirements. The following matrix outlines the available options:

Subject 

Assessment Model

CS1

Institution Control or IAI Control

CB1

Institution Control or IAI Control

CB2

Institution Control or IAI Control

CB3

Institution Control or IAI Control

CS2

IAI Control

CM1

IAI Control

CM2

IAI Control

Institution Control:

Under this mechanism, institutions follow the Accreditation Assessment Framework approved by the council. Evaluation involves preliminary screening and onsite visits to review pedagogy, question papers, and assessments. Institutions meeting accreditation criteria may conduct examinations independently, subject to periodic reviews by the IAI.

IAI Control:

Centralized assessment processes are managed by the IAI, ensuring standardized evaluation procedures across accredited institutions. An internal expert group is responsible for question paper setting, answer script marking, and result finalization. This approach provides institutions with support for academic enhancement and ensures the integrity of the examination process.

  • Benefits for IAI Control Institutions:

    Accredited institutions have access to a range of support services, including reference books, faculty training, and adjunct faculty onboarding. Leveraging IAI Subject Matter Experts for accreditation programs further enhances academic quality and ensures alignment with industry standards.

Our accreditation process is divided into two stages - Onboarding and Exemptions.

Stage 1: Onboarding

  1. Application Submission: Submit completed applications and supporting documentation, click here to access the application, Institution may choose the mode of control mechanism i.e., Institution or IAI control.
  2. Preliminary Screening: IAI shall perform initial screening and any additional information, shall be sought if required. If University/Institution passes the initial screening test, then IAI shall arrange for site visit to verify the information supplied in the application.

Stage 2: Accreditation & Exemptions

Upon successful completion of Stage 1, institutions proceed to Stage 2, where they continue with the Accreditation & Exemptions process. This stage involves a detailed assessment of the institution's program and potential granting of exemptions for specific subjects.

  • Formal Request: Institutions that qualify from Stage 1 submit formal requests for subject exemptions, outlining the specific subjects for which exemptions are sought.

  • Appointment of Independent Examiner: The IAI appoints an Independent Examiner to examine the University course and carry out subject mapping against IAI study material to identify the gaps in the course structure.

  • Course Structure Evaluation: If there are deficiencies/ inconsistencies in the course structure, the Independent Examiner collaborates with the institution to develop a revised structure aligned with the IAI syllabus.

  • Faculty Interaction: The Independent Examiner interacts with faculty members to understand the curriculum and teaching methodologies, especially for subjects where exemptions are sought.

  • Review of Examination Materials: Examination scripts, passing grades, and historical mark distributions for relevant courses are reviewed to assess the rigor and quality of assessment and decision on the par threshold.

  • Recommendations to IAI: Based on assessment, the Independent Examiner submits comprehensive recommendations to the IAI, including:

    • Course mapping with IAI syllabus.

    • Suggestions for changes in the course structure to closely align with IAI syllabus.

    • Recommendations on question paper formats, indicative solutions, and answer script standards.

    • Evaluation of faculty standards and potential support from the IAI.

  • Mapping and Evaluation: Syllabus objectives for exempted subjects are meticulously mapped to ensure alignment with the IAI syllabus. Independent Examiners remain collaboratively assigned to the institution to oversee the delivery of the program and the exemption recommendation process.

  • Assessment: Question papers, faculty qualifications, and other crucial parameters are thoroughly evaluated to ensure adherence to accreditation standards.

The Stage 2 process is exclusively designed to ensure institutions maintain high academic standards and alignment with the IAI syllabus, ultimately contributing to the enhancement of actuarial education and practice. Post qualification in both the stages, a MoU is signed between the IAI and the respective Institution.

Accreditation Renewal:

  1. The Accreditation Renewal will follow the same methodology as Initial Accreditation.
  1. Accreditation shall be for the period of maximum three (3) years. Six months before the expiry of accreditation, the revised assessment report will be screened by the respective authority for granting Re-Accreditation. Once the report is approved by the committee/group, the re-accreditation will be granted for a tenure of three years.

iai-soa-ifri-certificate-program.html:
Announcement on IAI and SOA International Financial Reporting Insurers (IFRI) Certificate Program

We are pleased to announce a momentous partnership between Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) and the Society of Actuaries (SOA), USA to introduce a standalone version of the SOA’s current International Financial Reporting for Insurers (IFRI) certificate program created specifically for actuaries working in India.

IFRS training is crucial for companies and professionals to ensure global financial reporting consistency, compliance with regulatory requirements and enhanced financial decision-making. In India, IFRS implementation has been on the horizon for several years, with regulatory bodies gradually converging Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) with IFRS to align with international standards. While the exact timeline for full IFRS implementation in India may vary, it is incumbent upon Indian businesses and professionals to prepare for the forthcoming transition.

This program is meticulously curated to cater to the needs of individuals actively engaged in IFRS implementation and practice in insurance sector. Furthermore, it is exceptionally well-suited for those working within or in collaboration with the actuarial or finance function, particularly in international or multinational insurance companies and financial, accounting and audit firms.

Program Overview:

This program is a comprehensive five-month training initiative that provides practical, hands-on training in the actuarial/financial elements of IFRS reporting requirements and IFRS 17 reporting standards applicable to insurance products. This end-to-end program includes self-directed and live learning experiences.

Program Structure:

The program includes six online e-Learning modules, two half-day online instructor-led virtual seminars, and an assessment. Successful participants will be conferred with a professional certificate jointly from IAI and SOA upon passing the final assessment.

E-learning Modules: Complete each of the six e-Learning modules with a self-assessment that measures comprehension and reinforces concepts and learning.

Live Concluding Seminars: The program concludes with two half-day online virtual instructor-led sessions.

Assessment: Complete the final ‘take-home’ assessment for an opportunity to earn certificate of recognition for the knowledge you’ve acquired.

Key Takeaways:

  • Acquire comprehensive coverage and thorough insights through a systematic approach, with key practical steps to support the organizational, financial, and reporting impacts of adopting IFRS 17, regardless of your organization’s stage of preparation or implementation.
  • Ideate and engage with program participants to discuss learning experiences, share results, and discuss course content.
  • Practice learned methods and concepts from a trusted source, with real-world illustrative examples and applications to grasp the shifts in reporting and their impact.
  • Obtain a certificate jointly from IAI and SOA upon the successful completion of the final assessment, providing recognition of the quantitative skills and comprehensive regulatory and reporting knowledge you have gained.

Registration:

The 2nd cohort registrations are LIVE upto 30th April 2024 till 3 pm. Upon successful registration, an email confirmation will be sent to the registered email address with the instructions.

Fee for Members

₹ 65,000 plus 18% GST extra

Fee for Non-Members

₹ 81,250 plus 18% GST extra

Point of Contact: For any queries, please write to “Ms. Swetha Jain” at swetha@actuariesindia.org and Ms. Gauri Jamwal at jamwal@actuariesindia.org.

Click here to register

 About the Institute of Actuaries of India

The Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament, viz. The Actuaries Act, 2006 for regulating the profession of Actuaries in India. The nodal ministry for the Institute is Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India. One of the objects of the Institutes is to promote, uphold and develop the standards of professional education, training, knowledge, practice and conduct amongst Actuaries. More information about IAI and on Actuaries can be found on IAI website at www.actuariesindia.org.

About the Society of Actuaries

With roots dating back to 1889, the SOA is the world’s largest actuarial professional organization with more than 32,000 actuaries as members. Through research and education, the SOA’s mission is to advance actuarial knowledge and enhance actuaries’ ability to provide expert advice and relevant solutions for financial, business, and societal challenges. The SOA’s vision is for actuaries to be the leading professionals in measuring and managing risk. Visit soa.org.

India-Fellowship-Seminar.html:

Institute of Actuaries of IndiaStatutory body under the Actuaries Act, 2006
About IFS Requirements MCQ Examination Transitional Provision Updates FAQs Result

Fellowship through the IAI Examination Route

The India Fellowship Seminar: Revised Format

Effective for candidates seeking admission as Fellow Members through the IAI Examination Route, Fellowship now requires two components — completed in a fixed order.

View the Two-Part Requirement Already attended IFS? Read the transitional provision

Order of completion

1

Professionalism MCQ Examination

Completed online. Must be successfully completed before registering for the IFS.

 
→
2

India Fellowship Seminar

One-day seminar. Completion is determined by verified attendance throughout its scheduled duration.

About IFS

Purpose of the IFS

The India Fellowship Seminar is a requirement for admission as a Fellow Member of the Institute of Actuaries of India. It provides professionalism education addressing ethics, governance, and India-specific regulation and practice relevant to the actuarial profession, and serves as a platform for deliberation on the standards expected of a Fellow.

The requirements described on this page apply to candidates seeking Fellowship through the IAI Examination Route. Candidates should confirm their own applicability against the Institute's official Announcement dated 27 August 2026.

Requirements

A Two-Part Requirement

Under the revised format, an eligible candidate is required to complete both of the following. Neither component, on its own, satisfies the requirement.

Step 1

Professionalism MCQ Examination

An online, multiple-choice examination conducted by the Institute. A candidate must successfully complete this examination before becoming eligible to register for the IFS.

  • Must be completed before IFS registration
  • Examination pattern and syllabus are set out under Professionalism MCQ Examination
  • Schedule, fees and registration process to be notified separately
Step 2

India Fellowship Seminar

A one-day seminar. Candidates attending for the purpose of admission as FIAI must remain present throughout its scheduled duration.

  • Completion is determined solely by verified attendance
  • There is no separate pass/fail assessment during the seminar

For the avoidance of doubt: successful completion of the Professionalism MCQ Examination does not, by itself, constitute completion of the IFS requirement, and attendance at the IFS does not, by itself, constitute successful completion of the revised requirements. A candidate seeking admission as FIAI through the IAI Examination Route must successfully complete both.

Completion of both requirements satisfies the applicable professionalism and seminar requirements only. Admission as FIAI remains subject to all other eligibility requirements prescribed by the Institute.

Step 1 of the Revised Format

Professionalism MCQ Examination

The examination is designed to assess candidates' understanding of professional conduct, ethics, governance, and regulatory requirements relevant to the actuarial profession.

Examination Pattern

Questions
30 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs)
Answer type
Single correct answer for each question
Maximum marks
30 1 mark per question
Duration
60 minutes
Negative marking
No
Passing score
60%

Syllabus

The examination will cover:

  • Professional Conduct Standards IAI Professional Conduct Standards (Version 4.0 / latest applicable version) Link
  • Act, Rules, Regulations & PoliciesActuaries Act, 2006 (“Act”) and the Rules, Regulations and Policies formed under the Act
  • GovernanceIAI Governance Structure, including Council, Committees & Advisory Groups, Quality Review Board, reporting relationships, and roles and responsibilities of governance bodies within the Institute
  • Disciplinary Process Relevant provisions of the Actuaries Act, 2006 (sections relating to misconduct and disciplinary proceedings) Link
  • Student Code of Conduct Code of Conduct for Students of the Institute of Actuaries of India Standards (Version 1.0 / latest applicable version) Link
  • APS/GN Coverage APS 9, APS 34 and other non-subject-specific APSs and Guidance Notes as may be notified by the Institute from time to time. Subject-specific APSs/GNs relating exclusively to Life Insurance, General Insurance, Health Insurance, Pensions, Investments or other specialised practice areas shall not form part of the syllabus unless specifically notified. Link

Frequency and Mode

Frequency
Ordinarily conducted quarterly, in January, April, July and October
Mode of examination
Online Home-based Proctored Examination

Results

Declaration of results
Declared within 15 working days from the date of examination
Marksheets and attendance certificates
Issued within 5 working days of declaration of results
Transitional Provision

Candidates Who Already Hold a Completion Certificate

Candidates who attended the 46th India Fellowship Seminar, or any earlier IFS, and were issued a Completion Certificate are not required to complete the Professionalism MCQ Examination for that already-satisfied requirement.

The validity of an existing Completion Certificate continues to be governed by the Institute's existing requirements:

  • a. Any remaining examination subjects must be passed within a maximum of three subsequent consecutive examination diets following the IFS.
  • b. Unless admitted as FIAI within twenty-four (24) months, counted from the month immediately succeeding the month of the IFS, the candidate must attend the IFS again and obtain a new Completion Certificate.

The requirement to complete the Professionalism MCQ Examination applies only to candidates who have not completed the 46th IFS, or an earlier IFS, prior to the effective date notified by the Institute.

Updates

Updates and Notifications


Professionalism MCQ Examination

The following will be notified separately by the Institute. This section will be updated as details become available — please check back rather than relying on unofficial sources.

  • Examination schedule and registration process
  • Examination fees
  • IFS seminar date
  • IFS registration process
  • Implementation timelines
FAQs

Common Questions

Do I need to complete both the MCQ Examination and the IFS?

Yes. A candidate seeking admission as FIAI through the IAI Examination Route must successfully complete both the Professionalism MCQ Examination and the IFS. Neither alone satisfies the requirement.

Can I register for the IFS before completing the MCQ Examination?

No. A candidate who has not successfully completed the Professionalism MCQ Examination is not eligible to register for the IFS.

Is the IFS itself assessed by an examination?

No. Completion of the IFS is determined on the basis of verified attendance throughout its scheduled one-day duration. There is no separate pass/fail assessment during the seminar.

I already hold a Completion Certificate from the 46th IFS or an earlier seminar. Do I need to take the MCQ Examination?

No, not for the purpose of satisfying the IFS requirement that you have already completed. The existing validity conditions attached to your Completion Certificate continue to apply — see the Transitional Provision above.

Where can I find the Professionalism MCQ Examination syllabus, schedule, and fees?

The examination pattern and syllabus are set out under Professionalism MCQ Examination. The examination schedule and fees have not yet been notified; the Institute will publish them separately, and this page will be updated accordingly.

Invitation for Expression of Interest (EOI)

Empanelment of Professors, Academicians and Professional Experts for Paper Setting and Marking of Core Principles Subjects

Submit Application Form Scope of Engagement

About the Institute of Actuaries of India

The Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI) is a statutory body established under the Actuaries Act, 2006, to regulate the actuarial profession in India. Among its key functions, IAI conducts professional examinations leading to qualification as Associate and Fellow actuaries. The examinations are held twice a year (each sitting is referred to as an “examination diet”) at centres in India and overseas, and are structured in four stages: Core Principles, Core Practices, Specialist Principles and Specialist Advanced.

Background and Objective

The Core Principles subjects form the technical foundation of the actuarial qualification and cover statistics, mathematics, data science, finance, economics and business management. With growing candidate numbers and an increasing emphasis on assessment quality, consistency and integrity, IAI wishes to broaden and strengthen its pool of subject matter experts by engaging eminent professors, academicians and professional experts.

Through this Expression of Interest, IAI invites professors and faculty members of the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) and other reputed universities and institutions, members of actuarial bodies, and experienced professionals to apply in their individual capacity for empanelment as experts for examination-related activities, primarily paper setting and marking of Core Principles subjects. The objectives of this engagement are to:

  • Enhance the academic rigour, quality and relevance of question papers;
  • Build a sustainable, diversified and independent pool of qualified paper setters and markers;
  • Improve the consistency and reliability of marking and standard setting across examination diets;
  • Strengthen collaboration between the actuarial profession, academia and industry experts;
  • Reduce dependence on a limited pool of examiners and ensure continuity of examination operations.

Subjects Covered

Applicants may express interest in one or more of the following Core Principles subjects. Detailed syllabi are available on the IAI website.

Code Subject Preferred Academic Background of Experts
CS1 Actuarial Statistics Statistics, Probability, Mathematical Statistics
CS2 Risk Modelling and Survival Analysis Statistics, Stochastic Processes, Survival Analysis, Biostatistics
CS3 Data Science: Tools, Techniques and Applications Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Analytics
CM1 Actuarial Mathematics for Modelling Actuarial Science, Financial Mathematics, Applied Mathematics
CM2 Economic Modelling Financial Economics, Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering
CB1 Business Finance Finance, Accounting, Corporate Finance
CB2 Business Economics Economics (Micro and Macro)
CB3 Business Management Management, Strategy, Organisational Behaviour
 
Note: For subjects that have both a theory paper (Part A) and a practical paper (Part B), support may be sought for either or both papers. Practical examinations are based on modelling in R and Excel.

Scope of Engagement

After empanelment and orientation by IAI, experts may be assigned one or more of the following activities:

Paper Setting:

Drafting original, syllabus-aligned question papers with appropriate coverage of learning objectives, cognitive levels and difficulty, along with detailed model solutions and marking schemes.

Question Paper Review and Quality Assurance:

Review of question papers to ensure syllabus coverage, accuracy, clarity, appropriate difficulty level, consistency and suitability within the prescribed examination duration.

Question Bank Development:

Contribution of high-quality questions for IAI’s secure question bank, particularly for computer-based and practical (R/Excel) examinations.

Marking (Evaluation):

Evaluation of candidate answer scripts (on-screen or physical) in line with the approved marking scheme and IAI marking guidelines.

Moderation and Check Marking:

Second marking, moderation of borderline scripts and consistency checks across markers.

Examiners’ Reports:

Preparation of post-examination reports highlighting candidate performance, common errors and guidance for future candidates.

Standard Setting and Review:

Participation in examiner meetings, pass mark discussions and review/re-evaluation processes, as required.

Capacity Building:

Participation in examiner seminars, training programmes and calibration sessions organised by IAI to enhance examination-related knowledge, marking consistency and assessment practices.

Examination-Related Advisory Support:

Providing subject-specific inputs and expert guidance to IAI on examination reforms, assessment methodologies, question paper standards and other academic matters, as required.

Who May Apply

  • Professors and faculty members (serving or retired) of IITs, IIMs, the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), National Institutes of Technology (NITs) and other Institutes of National Importance;
  • Academicians and researchers from reputed Central, State and Deemed Universities and colleges specialized in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Finance, Management, Data Science or Actuarial Science;
  • Fellows and Associates of IAI or other recognised actuarial bodies in India and overseas; particularly those engaged in teaching, academic activities, research or subject-related professional practice.
  • Academic Professionals from industry, regulatory or research organisations with proven expertise in the relevant subjects.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Ph.D. or Master’s degree in the relevant discipline, or Fellow/Associate membership of a recognised actuarial body;
  • Minimum 10 years of teaching, research or professional experience in the relevant subject area;
  • Prior experience in paper setting, evaluation, moderation or academic assessment for university-level or professional examinations will be preferred;
  • Proficiency in R and/or Excel for experts supporting practical (Part B) examinations, wherever applicable.
  • Applicants must not be involved in coaching, tutoring or preparing candidates for IAI examinations during the period of engagement, in accordance with IAI's conflict of interest guidelines.
  • Serving employees must obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) or necessary permission from their employer, where required under their applicable service rules.

Responsibilities of Empanelled Experts

  • Complete the orientation programme conducted by IAI and adhere to IAI's examination policies, SOPs, question paper setting guidelines, marking guidelines and prescribed timelines;
  • Remain available for assigned examination-related activities as per the examination calendar and complete the allocated work within the agreed timelines;
  • Ensure that all submitted work is original and free from plagiarism or unauthorised reproduction or reuse of published or copyrighted material;
  • Promptly disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest to IAI and comply with the applicable conflict of interest guidelines.
  • Promptly inform IAI of any change in availability, employment, institutional affiliation or other circumstances that may affect their engagement with IAI.

Confidentiality, Integrity and Conflict of Interest

  • All question papers, solutions, marking schemes, answer scripts and candidate data are strictly confidential and remain the exclusive property of IAI.
  • Every empanelled expert shall sign IAI’s Confidentiality Undertaking and Conflict of Interest Declaration before any assignment.
  • Experts shall not disclose their role as paper setter or marker for any specific subject or examination diet.
  • Experts whose relative or close associate is appearing in the same subject in the same examination diet must declare this and recuse themselves.
  • Examination material shall be handled only through secure channels prescribed by IAI and shall not be stored on personal or shared devices, except as permitted by IAI.
  • Any breach of confidentiality or integrity may lead to immediate disengagement, recovery of honorarium and appropriate legal action.

Honorarium and Terms of Engagement

  • Experts will be paid an honorarium directly, at IAI’s approved rates for paper setting, marking, moderation and related activities, as revised from time to time, subject to applicable tax deductions.
  • Engagement will initially be for a period of three years or six examination diets, whichever is earlier, renewable based on a performance review and IAI’s requirements.
  • Empanelment does not guarantee allocation of work; assignments will be made at IAI’s discretion based on requirements and expert profiles.
  • Terms of engagement will be formalised through an individual appointment letter issued by IAI to each empanelled expert.
  • Intellectual property in all examination material developed under this engagement shall vest exclusively with IAI.

Documents to be Submitted

  1. Completed Application Form (Annexure A)
  2. Detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  3. Copies of educational qualifications and professional memberships
  4. Evidence of relevant experience in paper setting, evaluation or other assessment activities (if any)
  5. No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the employer, where applicable
  6. Signed Declaration and Undertaking (Annexure B)

Evaluation and Selection Process

Applications will be evaluated by a committee constituted by IAI on the following indicative parameters:

S.no. Evaluation Parameter Weightage
1 Academic qualifications and professional credentials 25%
2 Subject expertise and relevant teaching, research or industry experience 30%
3 Prior experience in paper setting, evaluation and moderation 25%
4 Availability and range of subjects and activities offered 10%
5 Interaction with the evaluation committee and/or sample exercise 10%
Total 100%
 
Shortlisted applicants may be invited for an interaction and may be required to complete a sample paper-setting or marking exercise and attend orientation before final empanelment.

EOI Validity and Process Timeline (Continuous Process)

This EOI is a continuous activity and will remain open on a rolling basis, with no fixed closing date. Interested experts may apply at any time. Applications will be reviewed periodically in line with IAI’s examination calendar, and empanelled experts will be engaged for upcoming examination diets as required. IAI may review, update or withdraw this EOI at any time by publishing a notice on its website.

Activity Timeline
Issue of EOI 20/11/2026
Submission of EOI Open throughout the year (rolling basis)
Queries and clarifications May be raised at any time
Evaluation and shortlisting Periodically, at least twice a year (ahead of each examination diet)
Interaction with shortlisted applicants Within [4] weeks of each review cycle
Empanelment, appointment letter and orientation On an ongoing basis, before work is allocated
Allocation of work (paper setting / marking) As per the examination calendar for each diet
Review of empanelled experts Annually, or after every examination diet

General Terms and Conditions

library-services.title: Library Services
library-services.html:
The Library of IAI is very unique in its kind, as it has specialized collection to serve the information needs and provide guidance to those studying for actuarial examination. The library is the access point to get material for further reading in the subject of interest.

Circulation and Reader Service

  • Members who want to use the library services, can mail the library membership form to library@actuariesindia.org & sheetal@actuariesindia.org.
  • Members can borrow maximum two titles at a time. The duration for which a title can be kept is maximum 15 days for Mumbai based member and 21 days for outstation member.
  • Mumbai based members should come personally to collect the books, Out-station members can send their request through email and the book would be couriered to them.
  • The duration of loan can be extended by phone or e-mail or in person. Depending on the demand for the book it is reissued to the same person for 2 more weeks.
  • One can renew the title only one time for further 15 days before due date depending upon the demand of the same. Fine on late return is Rs. 10 per day.
  • One can reserve a book, which is out in circulation. As soon as the book returns to the library the person who has reserved the book will be intimated by e-mail or phone.
  • The documents which are for reference only can be accessed and photocopies of required part can be requested.
  • Members need to ensure safe return of the title to the library, failing which they will be required to bear the cost of the title or provide another fresh copy of same title to the library.
